analysis.summary: F-CLEAN-004: the Dexie schema and its v1→v2 upgrade callback are defined twice — once in src/dashboard/utils/db.js (lines 14-44) and once in src/lib/db-sw.js (lines 14-32) — with the SW file carrying a 'must match dashboard/utils/db.js' comment that is exactly the kind of cross-file coupling a shared module eliminates. The fix is one new file (src/db/schema.js) exporting the two store-strings plus the upgrade callback; both db.js and db-sw.js then import from it. The Dexie database name 'EchoFootPrint' is identical in both files and travels with the schema.
analysis.details: Current implementation: db.js and db-sw.js each call `new Dexie('EchoFootPrint')` and each define version(1) and version(2) with the same three stores (footprints, settings, geoCache) and the same v1→v2 upgrade (backfill platform='facebook' on every footprint, delete ipGeo). The dashboards-only file (db.js) adds a small handful of higher-level helpers (getFootprints with filter, getStats, calculatePlatformStats, checkStorageQuota, clearAllData, exportDatabase) that the SW does not need. The SW-only file (db-sw.js) adds sanitizeString / isValidDomain / getTodayFootprintCount that the dashboard does not need. Only the schema and the upgrade callback are duplicates. The natural split: new src/db/schema.js exports { DB_NAME, SCHEMA_V1, SCHEMA_V2, upgradeV2 } (or similar). Each Dexie wrapper keeps its own API but uses these constants: `new Dexie(DB_NAME).version(1).stores(SCHEMA_V1).version(2).stores(SCHEMA_V2).upgrade(upgradeV2)`. Verification per the issue body: `rg -n "db.version\(1\)" src/` should show exactly one definition site. Both definitions are in production code today; the unify is a pure refactor with zero behavior change.

decision_record.root_cause: F-CLEAN-004: the Dexie schema and v1→v2 upgrade are duplicated in src/dashboard/utils/db.js and src/lib/db-sw.js. The SW file even comments 'must match dashboard/utils/db.js', which is exactly the cross-file coupling a shared module eliminates.

Generate schema at build time (rejected: over-engineering for a four-store schema)
decision_record.selected_option: Create src/db/schema.js; both wrappers import from it
decision_record.residual_risk: Both wrappers must use the same DB_NAME. If one of them is updated and the other is not, the database becomes two real databases. The single-source fix removes that risk; the verify command (`rg -n "db.version\(1\)" src/` → one match) catches any re-introduction.
